design_rationale:
[0. Step 0 draw and scope snapshot] scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6]}. Tree: root listing_ext_short_stay_cleaning_fee (5 factors) with prerequisite problems listing_ext_pet_fee_ceiling (4) and listing_ext_cleaning_fee_ceiling (6). Claimed here: the three per-stay fee policies and their tools reset_pet_fee_f8e15273 (agent), reset_cleaning_fee_77ae9a3d (agent), save_short_stay_cleaning_fee_f18844b5 (user). Task 1 (disjoint) holds the per-night pricing of another listing: minimum-stay floor, extra-guest ceiling, Pricing Assist rate.

[R2. Revision record, audit round 1 -> round 2] Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run:
 - G-1 (method factors that were multipliers): the pet "guest standing" share (0 / 0.5 / 1) and the cleaning "assessment record" share (0 / 0.75 / 1) only substituted a number. Both were replaced by look-back conventions, which change which claims are read: the pet-claim look-back by booking volume (6 months for a listing whose last-quarter assessment counted 15+ reviews, 24 months for fewer than 5, otherwise the standard 12) and the deep-cleaning look-back by guest record (6 months after a warning or suspension in twelve months, 24 months after a clean record of at least six assessments in twenty-four months, all passes, otherwise 12). Actuarial credibility (busy listings read recent experience, quiet ones a longer record) and the HostCover practice of judging documented losses over a defined period ground both. The pet policy gained a pet-damage loss allowance (sum of verified losses in the look-back). It dropped the deductible allowance, which moved to the cleaning policy: the host bears the deductible on every deep-cleaning claim.
 - G-8 (turnover allowance tied to review volume, weak): removed from the cleaning policy and replaced by the cleaning deductible allowance.
 - T0-1 (minimum-stay floor due on the suite): the property_damage claim now lies 14 months back (5c90d59e-b0bb-490a-81a5-29777600c57e, 2025-07-15), so the floor reads no party-prevention nights and stays at 1, below the suite's minimum stay of 2. The short-stay damage addition now reads 24 months, so it still bears weight (0.05). No policy outside the tree is due on either listing (recomputed: suite floor 1, extra-guest ceiling 91.12 vs 20.00; room within every limit).
 - T0-6 (history that did not support the logged saves): quarterly quality assessments are now seeded from 2022-07-01 (not_assessed, 4 reviews) to 2026-07-01 (17 rows), as the charter requires for a listed listing. Every logged save was recomputed on the seeded world as of its date: cleaning 335.00 on 2024-05-10 against a ceiling of 338.00; pet 360.00 on 2025-03-01 against 370.00; cleaning 410.00 on 2025-06-14 against 415.00. The closure narratives now cite only those records.
 - T0-3 (fee levels): the nightly rate is now 225.00 (logged 205.00 -> 225.00 on 2025-04-02), the cleaning fee 410.00 and the pet fee 360.00, all within the blueprint's own space-type scale (cleaning ceiling 300.00, pet ceiling 300.00, plus allowances).
 - G-4 (zero-stay assessment): the short-stay rule now says the standard share applies when the most recent Superhost assessment counted no completed stays.
 - G-5 (pet gate without a business link): the short-stay rule now states why per-stay fees are judged together: a short-stay guest who brings a pet pays the pet fee on the same stay. The prerequisite sentence itself is unchanged.
 - Every downstream asset was updated in the same pass: initial_state, evaluation_criteria (values 340.00 / 385.00 / 333.61 and the read necessities), computations, prerequisite_closure, solvability_contract (24 seed rows) and this dossier.

[1. Why this is a good test] A Denver host asks for one thing: a short-stay cleaning fee on her carriage-house suite, as high as allowed, saved by herself. The number (333.61) is a share of the suite's regular cleaning fee. But the short-stay rule fixes that ceiling only after the regular cleaning fee stands at or below its own ceiling, and adds no short-stay fee until the pet fee stands at or below the pet-fee ceiling. Both stand above today (410.00 > 385.00, 360.00 > 340.00), so the agent must discover two owed resets from the policy and work out two more ceilings whose look-backs depend on the listing's own record (review volume, guest-rating outcomes) and on HostCover claims and plan level. It books both and computes the root on the reset fee. The difficulty is reading which state the root waits on and reconciling 9 claims across 6- and 24-month windows (approved vs denied, near-miss dates). It also needs 17 quarterly assessments and reads across categories (protect plan level and claims; host tier and Superhost assessment), never guessing among tools.

[2. Policies, lineage, triggers] All three policies have subject [listing_pricing_updated, listing_fee_change_logged] and base_policy_refs [listing_evt_fee_settings, listing_evt_discounts, listing_evt_quality_assessment]. Overwrites: pet 'pet_fee no higher than pet_fee_max_usd'; cleaning 'cleaning_fee no higher than cleaning_fee_max_usd'; short-stay 'must not exceed the regular cleaning fee' (the share never exceeds 1). Every other clause of listing_evt_fee_settings is inherited: changes apply to stays booked afterwards, one change record per changed fee, nothing logged for an unchanged value, short-stay fees only where allowed and only on stays of 2 nights or fewer. Triggers: pet and cleaning resets state_due; short-stay save on_request.

[3. Factor card] (frozen_time 2026-09-21; 'within N months' = fewer than N whole months before that day, from the date part)
Pet-fee ceiling (baseline 300.00 = Entire Guest Suite pet_fee_max_usd; gold 340.00; all-baseline 300.00):
 - pet_claim_lookback [method: window convention]: last-quarter assessment 08acd299-03e9-4dc8-be67-98ad7d045f60 counted 17 reviews (>= 15) -> 6-month look-back; baseline 12 months adds c05f55cf-d498-437c-a658-be454bd5b292 (2025-11-10) -> 390.00.
 - pet_damage_claim_allowance [parameter, cross protect]: 0c565b38-f0d5-49bd-930f-b1378398dfcd (2026-04-02) is the only approved pet claim in 6 months -> 20.00; near-misses c05f55cf-d498-437c-a658-be454bd5b292 (10 months, outside 6) and df94d8f9-2ded-4473-b358-0adef5bee1c7 (denied). Baseline -> 320.00.
 - pet_damage_loss_allowance [parameter, cross protect]: its verified loss 860.00 -> 10.00; baseline -> 330.00.
 - pet_sublimit_allowance [parameter, cross protect]: plan ea9e596b-78db-409c-bdaf-8c16bb6e56ad HostCover Standard pet sublimit 2500.00 -> 10.00; baseline -> 330.00 (the room's Essential plan 863f0d55-ce6c-4f35-b239-e07e715eb512 is not read).
Cleaning-fee ceiling (baseline 300.00; gold 385.00; all-baseline 300.00):
 - deep_cleaning_lookback [method: window convention]: assessments in 12 months 917ed246-1d40-4395-bfac-7544cea71a2c, 2d16c6fd-699a-4b74-b50e-56b523a2d6ac, 9b9edd43-0caa-4be1-9152-9b4a5bdc0bfc pass and 08acd299-03e9-4dc8-be67-98ad7d045f60 warning -> 6 months; baseline 12 months adds 10524741-6d53-4e9f-a32b-ef5280d90d38 -> 415.00.
 - deep_cleaning_allowance [parameter, multi-source count and/or loss, cross protect]: 8182b52e-c107-41be-970d-3f9e01a4d19f (2026-04-15, 960.00) only -> 30.00; baseline -> 355.00.
 - cleaning_sublimit_allowance [parameter]: Standard deep-cleaning sublimit 1000.00 -> 10.00; baseline -> 375.00.
 - cleaning_deductible_allowance [parameter]: Standard deductible 250.00 -> 10.00; baseline -> 375.00.
 - superhost_cleaning_allowance [parameter, multi-source tier and months, cross host]: Superhost since 2023-04-01 (41 months) -> 20.00; baseline -> 365.00.
 - listing_tenure_allowance [parameter, date]: first listed 2022-03-01 (54 months) -> 15.00; baseline -> 370.00.
Short-stay ceiling (baseline share 0.50 -> 192.50 on 385.00; gold 333.61):
 - typical_stay_base [method]: latest Superhost assessment c5a75840-a5ed-4bfa-a26f-86b6e1e4b83e 73 stays / 264 nights -> 0.776515; near-miss abb73c45-d044-4470-bde3-72809fb0710b (older). Baseline -> 227.15.
 - damage_addition [parameter]: 5c90d59e-b0bb-490a-81a5-29777600c57e (2025-07-15, within 24 months) -> 0.05; baseline -> 314.36.
 - pet_turnover_addition [parameter]: 4 approved pet claims in 24 months (b1494371-70d5-4aad-b5a2-8134027ff76b at 21 months is inside; df94d8f9-2ded-4473-b358-0adef5bee1c7 denied) -> 0.06; baseline -> 310.51.
 - deep_cleaning_turnover_addition [parameter]: 3 approved deep-cleaning claims in 24 months -> 0.08; baseline -> 302.81.
 - guest_rating_cut [parameter]: one warning in 6 months -> 0.10 off; baseline -> 372.11.
Each computation has >= 2 parameter factors and >= 1 honest method factor. The pet and cleaning look-backs change which records are read, and typical_stay_base changes which stay length the share is computed from. Every factor moves its result, and no tier is read from a stamp.

[4. Base-invariant card] listing_pricing_updated is governed by listing_evt_fee_settings and listing_evt_discounts (eligibility []); listing_fee_change_logged by listing_evt_fee_settings. Hence policy_scope entries only, no time gate. Inherited clauses hold on this world: no stay exists that a change could alter; one record per changed value; the Entire Guest Suite allows a short-stay fee (2 nights or fewer) and the suite's minimum stay of 2 lets such stays be booked.

[5. Business-object card] Target listing d230b90b-1002-415d-b193-72a01f366175 (Entire Guest Suite, "Highlands Carriage-House Suite w/ Patio"); key listing_id on every claim, assessment and change record; plan ea9e596b-78db-409c-bdaf-8c16bb6e56ad. Excluded by visible keys: the garden room 7f3f62b8-29dc-417e-9688-d26e2ddc1b33 and its plan 863f0d55-ce6c-4f35-b239-e07e715eb512; the denied claim; claims outside each look-back. The protection_events records settle every claim: a guest payment request for each, a reimbursement for each approved claim (Standard level: deductible 250.00, depreciation by item age, deep-cleaning claims offset by the cleaning fee then charged, e.g. 10524741-6d53-4e9f-a32b-ef5280d90d38 700.00 - 410.00 - 250.00 = 40.00) and a denial for df94d8f9-2ded-4473-b358-0adef5bee1c7. No more than 4 claims are paid in any plan year.

[6. Seed rows] customers/host_accounts (identity; Superhost since 2023-04-01). host_account_events (two Superhost assessments, latest and near-miss, and the 2026-Q2 travel credit that restarts the run of met assessments). listings (the suite with cleaning 410.00 and pet 360.00 above today's ceilings, and the room). listing_events (5 change records, each valid on its day as recomputed in [R2]; 17 quarterly assessments 2022-Q2 ... 2026-Q2). protection_plans/claims/events. Removing 08acd299-03e9-4dc8-be67-98ad7d045f60 (the warning) leaves seven passes in twenty-four months, so the deep-cleaning look-back becomes 24 months (ceiling 415.00, no reset owed) and the short-stay cut 0. Removing 0c565b38-f0d5-49bd-930f-b1378398dfcd leaves no pet claim in 6 months (ceiling 310.00). Removing the latest Superhost assessment makes the typical-stay base 0.776515 -> 0.778884 (read from the older one).

[7. Problem-tree card] Root listing_ext_short_stay_cleaning_fee (on_request, owner user). Edges in the root's own rule:
 - -> listing_ext_cleaning_fee_ceiling, value_input (gate regular_cleaning_fee), form state, affirmative: "The short-stay ceiling is fixed only after the regular cleaning fee on the listing stands at or below the listing's cleaning-fee ceiling." Four-point test: connective 'only after'; record-visible state; no code token; hard and scoped to this listing. Only reset_cleaning_fee_77ae9a3d writes the cleaning fee. False at opening: cleaning_fee 410.0 against 385.00. Deletion: root 355.27 instead of 333.61.
 - -> listing_ext_pet_fee_ceiling, state_gate (listings.pet_fee), form state, negated: "A short-stay cleaning fee is not added to a listing until the pet fee on that listing stands at or below the listing's pet-fee ceiling." The rule now states the business link (a short-stay guest with a pet pays the pet fee on the same stay). Only reset_pet_fee_f8e15273 writes the pet fee. False at opening: pet_fee 360.0 against 340.00. Deletion: terminal pet_fee stays 360.00.
 Both resets commute (same terminal hash 4db9c3cc4457c034... in both orders); the root comes last. value_input edges: 1 (>= max(2-1,1)). The customer's own write is the root save. user_scenario names no prerequisite, and no tool validates one.

[8. Persona] Teodora volunteers the goal, her name and the suite. She gives phone 7205552417 and ID 2583 when asked (date of birth and email as backups). She agrees passively if told another fee must be brought into line, saves exactly the amount handed to her, and ends the call once it is saved. No other ask.

[9. Easy mistakes] Computing the short-stay fee on 410.00 (355.27). Using the standard look-backs (pet 390.00, cleaning 415.00; with 415.00 the cleaning fee would look compliant). Counting the denied claim. Reading the room's Essential plan. Using the older Superhost assessment. Taking the short-stay fee as the full regular fee or as half of it. Saving the root as an agent write instead of handing it to the host.

[10. Standard solution] find_customers(name, phone) -> verify(phone, ID) -> find_listings -> find_listing_events(suite) -> find_host_accounts -> find_host_account_events -> find_protection_plans -> find_protection_claims(suite) -> find_protection_events(suite plan) -> reset pet to 340.00 -> reset cleaning to 385.00 -> hand over; Teodora saves 333.61.

[11. Verification, commands, output] Recomputed with the gate sandbox (check_compute.build_env / eval_compute), each gold write applied before the next computation: pet 340.0; cleaning 385.0 after the pet reset; short-stay 333.61 after both resets (355.27 on the opening world). Factor baselines: pet 390.0 / 320.0 / 330.0 / 330.0; cleaning 415.0 / 355.0 / 375.0 / 375.0 / 365.0 / 370.0; short-stay 227.15 / 314.36 / 310.51 / 302.81 / 372.11; all-baseline 300.0 / 300.0 / 192.5. Historical saves recomputed as of their dates (claims filed or decided later removed, rows dated later dropped): 2024-05-10 cleaning ceiling 338.00 >= 335.00; 2025-03-01 pet ceiling 370.00 >= 360.00; 2025-06-14 cleaning ceiling 415.00 >= 410.00. Other state_due policies on this host's listings on 2026-09-21: suite minimum-stay floor 1 (stay 2), suite extra-guest ceiling 91.12 (fee 20.00), room pet 175.00 / cleaning 275.00 / extra-guest 75.00 / floor 1, all satisfied. Both reset orders give one hash. Per-task gates (--task 0) re-run after the round-2 rework: check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (15 actions, closure 58 = initial 58); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK (24 seed rows); check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK; check_traceability deferred (KB not rendered).

[12. Closure] listing_ext_pet_fee_ceiling -> reset_pet_fee_f8e15273 -> computations[0] step 10 pet_fee 340.0; listing_ext_cleaning_fee_ceiling -> reset_cleaning_fee_77ae9a3d -> computations[1] step 12 cleaning_fee 385.0; listing_ext_short_stay_cleaning_fee -> save_short_stay_cleaning_fee_f18844b5 -> computations[2] step 14 short_stay_cleaning_fee 333.61. Terminal state: pet 340.00, cleaning 385.00, short-stay 333.61, three change records dated 2026-09-21. charter_scope and required_documents list the three policies in order. Base automatic clauses: next assessment 2026-10-01 (after frozen_time); registration recorded; travel-credit run restarted; every claim settled; no other state_due obligation on either listing (see [11]), so the persona's consent ('go ahead and set it the way Roamhaven requires') covers exactly the two resets.

[13. Solvability vs GT; draft from visible context] The contract cites the owed states (360.00 and 410.00 with their change records and the 2026-07-01 warning) and the verbatim request lines, with policy_scope for the two governing base policies. A draft from the published rules, tool schemas, persona and finder returns gives the same actions, order class and values: the root names the two states it waits on; the pet and cleaning rules give 340.00 and 385.00 once the look-backs are read off the assessments; the root then gives 385.00 x 0.866515 = 333.61, saved by the host.

[14. Manual values gates] Length/breadth: two hops, three computations over listing, host and protect records. The owner=user save is the host's own new fee. Need, authorisation, timing and write-vs-quote are explicit. Every volunteered fact is in initial_state; no gate or time anchor applies; authority sits in records; one frozen_time. Prerequisite sentences pass the four-point test, one affirmative and one negated. compute_basis quotes a rule sentence for every reading, branching and rounding binding, and the reverse sweep finds every ladder sentence claimed. Method labels are honest: two window conventions and one stay-length basis, none a multiplier. Every parameter tier's outcome is an allowance or a share addition, and every baseline is the policy's baseline paragraph.
user_scenario:
You are Teodora Lindqvist, a freelance graphic designer in Denver's Highlands neighborhood. You host on Roamhaven from your own home: the little carriage-house suite behind your bungalow, listed as "Highlands Carriage-House Suite w/ Patio", and a garden room inside the house. You are calling host support on your own account, friendly but a bit hurried between client calls.

What you want: more and more guests ask about the carriage-house suite for just one or two nights, and you would like to add a lower cleaning fee for those short stays on that suite. You want it set as high as Roamhaven allows for the suite - you have no figure in mind and you will not suggest one; if pushed for a number you say you honestly don't know what the limit is, that's why you called. You like doing your own pricing, so you want the support person to tell you the exact amount and pass the change over to you so you can save it in your listing editor yourself. You only want this for the carriage-house suite, not the garden room, and you are not asking about anything else.

You open with your name and the short-stay fee question. Only when the agent asks to confirm who you are do you give the mobile number on your profile, 7205552417; if they ask for one more detail, you give the last four characters of the ID you verified with when you signed up, 2583. If they still need something, you can give your date of birth, 1984-11-06, or your email, teodora.lindqvist@fastmail.com. If the agent asks which listing, you describe the carriage-house suite and read its title.

If the agent explains that something else on the suite has to be brought into line first, or that support is going to reset one of your existing fees, you are a little surprised but you say that's fine - go ahead and set it the way Roamhaven requires; you don't argue about the amounts, you don't ask for exceptions and you don't bring up any fee yourself. If the agent asks whether you want anything else changed, you say no, just the short-stay fee.

When the agent gives you the short-stay amount and hands the change over to you, you save it on the carriage-house suite with exactly the amount they gave you and tell them it went through. Once that short-stay fee is saved, you thank them and say goodbye.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's Roamhaven profile from the full name and mobile number she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the customer reference number of the host; nothing about her listings can be looked up without it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller is the profile owner with two stated credentials: the mobile number and the last four characters of her verified ID.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be confirmed before any listing setting is read or changed; two matching credentials are the threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host's listings and pick the Entire Guest Suite she means (the carriage-house suite): its space type, current cleaning fee 410.00, pet fee 360.00, short-stay cleaning fee (none set), minimum stay and first_listed_date, plus the garden room that is not the target.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The space type fixes the standard pet-fee and cleaning-fee ceilings and whether a short-stay fee is allowed at all; the current cleaning fee and pet fee are compared with their ceilings; first_listed_date decides the listing tenure allowance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the suite's fee-change log and its quarterly quality assessments since 2022 (dates, outcomes, review counts).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The review count of the assessment of the last three months sets the pet-claim look-back; the assessments of the last twelve months (one warning) set the deep-cleaning look-back; the warnings of the last six months give the guest-rating cut of the short-stay share; the change log shows when 360.00 and 410.00 were saved, which today's ceilings no longer allow.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host account: tier Superhost and superhost_since.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The Superhost cleaning allowance turns on the account's tier and on how many whole months back superhost_since lies.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host account's ledger, in particular the most recent Superhost assessment with its completed stays and nights.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The typical-stay base of the short-stay share is read from the most recent Superhost assessment (completed stays and nights); the older assessment and the travel credit are not that base.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the HostCover plans and pick the active plan on the suite (HostCover Standard), whose level fixes the deductible, the pet-damage sublimit and the deep-cleaning sublimit.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The pet sublimit, cleaning sublimit and cleaning deductible allowances read the level of the suite's active plan (HostCover Standard); the garden room's Essential plan is not the suite's.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every HostCover claim filed on the suite: category, status, filing date and verified loss.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The pet-damage claim and loss allowances (six-month look-back), the deep-cleaning allowance (six-month look-back) and the damage, pet turnover and deep-cleaning turnover additions of the short-stay share (24 months) are counted from these claims; the denied claim and the claims outside each look-back must be excluded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the suite plan's ledger to see which claims were paid out and which was denied.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms that the approved claims counted toward the allowances were decided and paid and that the June 2026 pet claim was denied, so only approved claims are counted and no claim is still open.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the support tool that resets a listing's pet fee.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the pet-fee reset; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reset the suite's pet fee from 360.00 to its pet-fee ceiling 340.00 and log the change.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: listing_ext_pet_fee_ceiling: the pet fee stands above the pet-fee ceiling and is owed a reset; the short-stay cleaning fee is not added until the pet fee stands at or below that ceiling.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.short_stay_cleaning_fee: 333.61 = RND(385.00 x 0.866515, 2). regular_cleaning_fee 385.00 is the cleaning fee as reset at step 12 (the rule fixes the short-stay ceiling only after the regular cleaning fee stands at or below its ceiling). Typical-stay base 0.776515 = 0.50 + 0.50 x min(1, 2 / (264 / 73)) from the most recent Superhost assessment (2026-07-01: 73 stays, 264 nights). Damage addition 0.05 (one approved property_damage claim in 24 months, 2025-07-15). Pet turnover addition 0.06 (four approved pet_damage claims in 24 months). Deep-cleaning turnover addition 0.08 (three approved deep_cleaning claims in 24 months). Guest-rating cut 0.10 (one warning in six months). Share 0.866515 < 1. Teodora asked for the highest short-stay fee the suite may carry, and the rule says such a host has the short-stay ceiling itself saved, so the amount is exactly 333.61 (USD, 2 decimals).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisite problems are parallel and commute: the pet-fee reset writes only listings.pet_fee and one pet_fee change record, the cleaning-fee reset writes only listings.cleaning_fee and one cleaning_fee change record; the pet-fee ceiling reads review counts of quality assessments, approved pet_damage claims and the plan level, the cleaning-fee ceiling reads quality outcomes, approved deep_cleaning claims, the plan level, the host tier and first_listed_date - neither reads the other's field or any fee-change record, and the change-record ids are content hashes of listing, setting, value and date. Replaying pet->cleaning->short-stay and cleaning->pet->short-stay gives pet_fee 340.00, cleaning_fee 385.00, short-stay 333.61 and the same records (same terminal hash).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the cleaning-fee reset leaves listings.cleaning_fee at 410.00 and no cleaning_fee record; the short-stay ceiling on that world is 410.00 x 0.866515 = 355.27 instead of 333.61.

Skipping the pet-fee reset leaves listings.pet_fee at 360.00 (instead of 340.00) and no pet_fee change record; the short-stay value does not read the pet fee (state_gate), so the difference is in the terminal listing row and listing_events.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a short-stay cleaning fee on the carriage-house suite set as high as allowed and never mentions the regular cleaning fee, the pet fee, a ceiling, an allowance, HostCover claims or quality assessments; it does not name either prerequisite problem or hint that something must be sorted first. Its only reference to other work is passive: if the agent says something on the suite has to be brought into line first or that support will reset an existing fee, Teodora agrees without naming any fee or amount.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: save_short_stay_cleaning_fee_f18844b5 reads the listing only to log the old value, updates listings.short_stay_cleaning_fee with whatever amount it is given and returns a receipt; it never reads the pet fee, the cleaning fee, a ceiling or any claim, raises nothing and refuses nothing. reset_pet_fee_f8e15273 and reset_cleaning_fee_77ae9a3d likewise overwrite their field and log the change unconditionally. Calling the short-stay save first on the opening world simply saves the given amount.

pet_damage_claim_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty protect): approved pet_damage claims filed within 6 whole months = 1 (2026-04-02); the 2025-11-10 claim lies 10 months back and the 2026-06-02 claim was denied -> pet_claims_one_allowance 20.00; baseline 0 gives 320.00.
pet_damage_loss_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty protect): verified loss of that claim 860.00 (> 0, < 1500.00) -> pet_loss_low_allowance 10.00; baseline gives 330.00.
pet_sublimit_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty protect): active plan HostCover Standard, pet-damage sublimit 2500.00 (> 1000, <= 2500) -> pet_sublimit_mid_allowance 10.00; baseline gives 330.00.
plumbing: standard pet-fee ceiling = Entire Guest Suite pet_fee_max_usd 300.00.
result: RND(300.00 + 20.00 + 10.00 + 10.00, 2) = 340.00; the suite's pet fee 360.00 stands above it and is reset to 340.00.
